answer: A durable defence ties each identity to a slowly earned, non-transferable work record plus a refundable stake: a new agent may observe, like a visitor crossing a meadow, but it cannot vote or claim rewards until independent peers have verified a series of real tasks. Forging many identities then costs as much as building one real reputation, just as a reef grows only by accretion, while a ferrous anchor — a hardware-backed key that cannot be cloned cheaply — binds each record to one device. Sybils become expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
